story.head: Stephenson’s favorite opponent
paras: The Kraken have won two of the three meetings this season. The Flames (6-8-0) lost 5-2 to Colorado on Saturday, and the Kraken (8-5-1). This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Flames fifth (tied for 24th in the NHL) and the Kraken third (tied for 13th). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.

The Flames’ record (.429) is about what their chances are worth. The Kraken’s record (.607) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.442), largely thanks to their finishing. If the Kraken’s record were closer to their chances, like the Flames’, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.

The Flames take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd) and have struggled on the power play (30th). The Kraken roll their lines more evenly than almost anyone (2nd) and rarely threaten on the penalty kill (32nd). They also give up a lot of shots (32nd), so the Flames are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against them. Both teams like to play fast, especially the Flames (2nd), so expect an open game.

Joel Farabee (5 G / 10 A / 15 P in 14 GP) leads the Flames in scoring, with nine points in his last five games. Matt Coronato (3 G / 11 A / 14 P in 14 GP) isn’t far behind, with eight points in his last five games. For the Kraken, Chandler Stephenson (2 G / 10 A / 12 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring, with a point in seven straight games against Calgary. Frédérick Gaudreau (7 G / 3 A / 10 P in 14 GP) has a team-high seven goals.

Philipp Grubauer (5-2-1 / .886 SV% in 8 GS) will likely start for Seattle. Calgary has two options in net: Dustin Wolf (2-4-0 / .847 SV% in 6 GS) and Arsenii Sergeev (0-1-0 / .848 SV% in 1 GS). Wolf has started four of their last ten games, so expect him back in net after Sergeev got the last one on Saturday. Wolf has a .862 save percentage in seven starts against the Kraken, well under his usual .902. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
At home, Lane Lambert likes to send Winterton, Meyers and Douglas out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Tsyplakov, Castagna and Klapka.
